text:
sanjay: runtime alert: spike in per-key 429s across multiple orgs starting ~09:12 UTC. Dashboards show sudden drop in allowed tokens for many keys. Linking runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/rate-limits

deploy-bot: deploy finished: quota-reconciler v2.1.3 at 2026-03-18T09:10:05Z by alex :white_check_mark:

maria: on it. any sample 429 logs? short stack/traces would help

sanjay: here's a typical response we see in logs (sanitized):
```json
{"ts":"2026-03-18T09:13:21Z","org":"org-42","api_key":"sk-***","path":"/v1/generate","status":429,"error":"per_key_quota_exceeded","details":{"limit":"0","window_s":"60"}}
```

alex: looking at reconciler diff now. immediate suspicion: a change in default handling for missing quota rows. new code sets missing -> 0 instead of inheriting legacy. snippet: 
```py
def reconcile(row):
    burst = row.get('burst', 0)  # oops, previously we used stored_default_burst
```
This will zero out any org without an explicit quota entry.

maria: that would explain it. Which environments got the new reconciler? prod only?

alex: prod and staging. Staging had guard rails but prod ran the migration without the backfill flag. I missed the backfill check in the rollout.

sanjay: impact: affected ~120 orgs, many small customers seeing immediate 429s -> clients falling back to multi-model routing -> latency and cost spike. Console alerts triggered for surge in fallback pool and error budget burn.

ops-bot: runbook: disable reconciler job (cron) and restore last stable quota snapshot. Command: 
```
kubectl set env deployment/quota-reconciler DISABLED=true -n infra
redwood infra snapshots restore --name=quota-snapshot-2026-03-17T23:00Z
```

maria: doing the restore now. pausing reconciler and re-applying snapshot. will monitor for cleared 429s.

alex: pushing hotfix to change default to use stored_default_burst and require explicit 0 to mean blocked. quick patch: 
```diff
- burst = row.get('burst', 0)
+ burst = row.get('burst') if 'burst' in row else stored_default_burst
```
I'll open a PR and cut a canary deploy to prod after snapshot restore.

sanjay: support: please notify affected customers with high priority template (use incident type=quota-regression). Ticket created: PM-2391. 

support-bot: paging on-call support and adding incident tag: quota_regression, severity=3

maria: post-restore check: 429 rates dropped to baseline within 4 mins. fallback traffic dropped accordingly. still doing org-by-org verification and running a backfill to ensure no other missing entries get 0.

sanjay: root cause summary for now: reconciler migration defaulted missing quotas to 0. Immediate remediation: disable job and restore snapshot. Next actions: hotfix + safe rollout gating + add unit test for missing-key handling + console alert that flags mass-zero quota changes.

alex: sorry about the rollout gap, taking ownership for the PR and follow-ups.

maria: creating follow-up checklist in the incident ticket with owners and ETA for fixes.

sanjay: thanks team. closing the high-alert after 1h once backfill completes; will post full postmortem to PM-2391.
